gems.name: diamond
gems.note: The unrefracted seventh. A cool near-white, not #FFFFFF, so it reads as luminous rather than flat.

reserved.pink: ABSENT BY CONSTRUCTION. Reserved for B-Dating and romantic contexts. It is not an oversight and must not be filled in.

siteValues.name: violet-sey
siteValues.note: NOT an eighth gem. The commons' medium is not one of the seven, so borrowing amethyst would overload a channel the doctrine reserves. The measured reason agrees: those pages are read at arm's length outdoors and the more saturated violet survives sunlight.

$comment: The aura ramp. SEMANTICS ONLY — no hex values live here. The hexes are
in css/tokens.css (--color-aura-red and siblings) and are joined onto
this map by scripts/generate.mjs, exactly as gems.json is joined. Read
dist/tokens.json for the joined result.
⚠️ THIS IS A RATE MAP. A colour here means a POSITION — how fast a
person's gratitude is circulating — not a medium (that is gems.json)
and not a domain (that is tlds.json). Three palettes; seven, seven and
six; and the hues rhyme because a colour wheel is small. Never present
any two of them as one system.
⚠️ THE SEVENTH IS VIOLET, NOT DIAMOND. This ramp and the gem palette
both have seven stops and they are DIFFERENT SETS: this one carries
indigo and ends at violet; the gems carry no indigo and end at the
unrefracted diamond. The shared count is a coincidence.
⚠️ DISCRETE, NOT CONTINUOUS. colorFor() returns a bucket NAME, so a
person is in exactly one stop and never between two. That is what
makes seven flat tokens the right shape here. The Metta Light — the
gem-order descent named in gems.json — is the continuous one, driven
by a single 0-to-1 scalar. Do not build this one as a gradient.
auras.meaning: Circulation velocity, computed as crossings per month over a rolling window and bucketed server-side.
auras.source: thank.heartbank.org/functions/src/auras/compute.ts — COLOR_BUCKETS is canonical for the thresholds; this file is canonical for the colours.
auras.twoRings: A person carries TWO auras at once — one for Kiitos (gratitude shown) and one for Kiitti (kindness given). Same ramp, two independent positions.

buckets.name: indigo
buckets.note: ⚠️ FOUR SHIPPED SURFACES RENDERED THIS BUCKET IN PINK — members-panel.ts, seed, thank and timelog reached for bg-pink-100/text-pink-400 while the three hex maps said #4f46e5. Pink is reserved by construction for B-Dating and must not appear on a Phase-1 surface. Corrected to indigo. If the reason was that blue-indigo-violet are hard to tell apart at tint weight, the fix is to widen the ramp here, where one change reaches every surface — never to borrow the reserved hue on four of them.

reserved.pink: ABSENT HERE FOR THE SAME REASON IT IS ABSENT FROM THE GEMS — held for B-Dating and romantic contexts. This ramp is where the reservation was actually being violated.

collisions: Both are coincidence, not kinship. Three names, three meanings; do not alias them, or re-tuning one will silently move the others.

$comment: The six-TLD rainbow. NAMES ONLY, AND THAT IS THE POINT — unlike gems.json
and auras.json, this file has no sibling hexes in css/tokens.css to be
joined against, because none have ever been assigned. The corpus fixes the
six COLOURS as words (brand-identity-as-architecture §6.4 and §10.1,
resolved 2026-06-30); no file in the estate fixes a value.
⛔ DO NOT PIN HEXES HERE TO MAKE THE PAGE PRETTIER. Nothing consumes them:
the four sites that vendor this layer are sayyourname, playsey, seysays and
333.eco, and not one of them is a heartbank.{TLD}. Six tokens would ship
byte-identical into all four behind brand.lock, buy nothing, and invite
exactly the misuse the gem warning already forbids. Pin them when the first
heartbank.{TLD} surface actually needs them, and measure contrast then —
the gem palette's own hexes were proposed in a working document and lived
there for weeks before they were ratified into tokens.css.
⚠️ THIS IS A DOMAIN MAP. A colour here means a DOMAIN's product class and
its heart-idiom — not a medium (gems.json) and not a rate (auras.json).
The six hues are one-for-one with the six saturated gems, which is exactly
why they are rendered on a different CARRIER on the guidelines page: gems
are chips, these are marks. Same hue, different object, no fusion.
`cssNamed` below is the CSS keyword that spells the doctrine's word. It is
a RENDERING OF THE NAME, never a pinned value — that is why it is a
keyword and not a hex, and why it is allowed to look untuned beside the
measured gems.
tlds.order: Spectrum order, red through violet. The assignments were made per-domain, one at a time, by heart-idiom — that they compose a complete rainbow was found afterwards, and showing them out of spectrum order would hide the only property that makes the allusion earned.
tlds.scope: HeartBank® — one body of five. This palette is body-scoped in a way the gems and the aura ramp are not; it is documented here because the brand layer is where the three palettes are told apart, not because the institution's colour system is one body's domain map.

motion.signature: Cardiac morphology: two UNEQUAL beats then a long rest — systole, a weaker diastole, then most of the period at rest.
motion.notRate: The RHYTHM is the signature, NOT the cadence or the amplitude. ~40 BPM at 1.5s ships; a 72 BPM variant was built and rejected. A published spec once claimed ~72 BPM / ~8% expansion — that claim was reframed, not the code.
motion.rest: The diastolic rest is IN THE KEYFRAMES (70%->100%, 450ms of every 1500ms), recurring on every cycle. It is not --beat-delay, which is a CSS animation-delay and fires once before the first iteration only. Both produce stillness; only the keyframe rest is part of the rhythm.
motion.startDelay: --beat-delay is 0s as of v1.3.0. It was 1.5s, which bought nothing recurring and left a Proof-of-Humanity signal motionless for a beat and a half after paint. The token is kept for per-instance STAGGER, so several marks on one screen need not beat in lockstep.
motion.reducedMotion: Stop, and substitute nothing. The static mark is already a meaningful state.

mettaLight.$comment: The session descent. css/metta.css is OPT-IN and is not vendored by a surface with no session.
mettaLight.api: The app sets --t (0 at session start, 1 at session end) on an element carrying the .metta class. Everything downstream reads --metta.
mettaLight.stops: The B-Gem order, ruby to diamond. Seven stops, six segments; stop i sits at t = i/6.
mettaLight.notAnimated: --metta is COMPUTED, never animated. An @property-registered custom property interpolated by @keyframes is the obvious build and is broken in the configuration this feature requires: Chrome does not reliably re-rasterise an element for an animated custom property it INHERITS, and the failure is invisible to getComputedStyle. Six color-mix() steps weighted by clamp() windows instead — no registration, no keyframes, no ticker.
mettaLight.classScoped: The chain is declared on .metta and NOT on :root. Custom properties inherit their computed value, so a chain on :root resolves once against root's --t and descendants inherit a frozen colour. The element that sets --t must carry the chain.
mettaLight.guards: No numerals, no totals, no streaks, no ranks. The light carries the whole signal; --t is an input, never a readout.
mettaLight.breathNotHeartbeat: The lamp's swell is a symmetrical breath with no claim attached. The heartbeat is a Proof-of-Humanity signal with a placement rule. Never give the lamp .beating, and never give a mark the breath. Under reduced motion the breath stops and the COLOUR DOES NOT — freezing the descent would misreport where the sitter is.
mettaLight.nativePorting: Same seven stops, same single scalar: interpolate the gem list at t. That is why it belongs in platform-native animation rather than a library.

accentRule.rule: A site's accent is DERIVED, never picked: it takes the gem whose media type IS that product's medium.
cannotDerive: --accent-ink — Fire Opal on white is 3.4:1 and fails; Sapphire on white is 7.0:1 and passes. No formula picks correctly.
--accent-soft on a light ground — the generic oklab mix does not always clear 4.5:1. Measure and pin.
accentRule.honestCount: The goal was 'a fifth site is five declarations'. It is nine.

mark.name: B-Emblem™
mark.shape: A universal heart rotated 45° clockwise. Bistable — heart AND capital B, both immediately apparent. Not a reveal.
rules: Inline in the DOM. Never — CSS cannot reach inside an .
The 45° rotation is baked into the path coordinates. Never a transform attribute.
`.beating` goes on CHROME and never beside a person's name.

states.static: Proof of Coordinate ℠ — a meaningful state, not a degradation.
states.beating: Proof of Humanity ℠ — but only where the beat can be verified. Ambient institutional beating claims 'humans run this', not 'this person is human'.

wordmark.division: Bank = what accumulates is the RECORD of appreciation. Heart = what circulates is the VALUE.
wordmark.substitution: Wherever possible the B in 'Bank' is replaced by the B-Emblem — 'Thank with Heart♥ank®'. Only the B in Bank, never the T in Thank. Monochrome and plain-text fall back to a literal B.
